Context/Background: In a prospective endometrial carcinoma (EC) cohort, we performed a differential analysis of protein levels between hotspot-mutated CTNNB1 and WT CTNNB1 tumors, in the CNV-L subgroup.  In a separate analysis, we found that CTNNB1 S45 phosphorylation was significantly downregulated in hotspot-mutated tumors, whereas phosphosites distant from the hotspot mutations were mostly upregulated.
Prompt: Provide a discussion of the results from the differential analysis and any relevance to the mutation state of CTNNB1.

Introduction/Context  
A quantitative proteomic comparison was performed on CNV-L endometrial carcinomas harboring hotspot CTNNB1 mutations versus CTNNB1 wild-type (WT).  The dataset comprises 10 150 measured proteins; differential‐abundance statistics (log₂FC, T-score, P‐value, FDR) were computed (csv_id 1765760705_bb7aad74).  Among Wnt pathway components, CTNNB1 itself is significantly upregulated in hotspot mutants (L2FC = 0.76, FDR = 1.7×10⁻¹¹), consistent with reduced degradation.  In prior phosphoproteomic analysis, S45‐phosphorylation of CTNNB1 was downregulated, indicating altered post-translational control.  Other specifics (number of tumors, replicates, clinical covariates) were not specified.

Analysis  
Hotspot mutations in CTNNB1 lead to stabilization and higher abundance of β-catenin (L2FC = 0.76, FDR < 1×10⁻¹⁰), paralleled by upregulation of Wnt targets AXIN1, DKK4 (L2FC = 4.05), LEF1 (L2FC = 1.31) and receptors (LRP4).  GSEA reveals robust upregulation of protein‐folding/ER processing, translational machinery (ribosome, rRNA processing), mitochondrial gene expression and OXPHOS—hallmarks of increased biosynthetic and energy demands in CTNNB1-mutant EC.  Conversely, innate immunity and extracellular matrix–related programs (complement cascades, inflammatory response, cilium assembly, myogenesis, EMT) are suppressed, suggesting immune evasion and altered differentiation.  The downregulated EMT signature in mutants is notable given CTNNB1’s role in cell–cell adhesion and transcriptional regulation.

Targeted Subset  
Filtering GSEA outputs for “Wnt” or CTNNB1‐related terms returned the colorectal cancer pathway (KEGG hsa05210, NES 2.02) as mildly enriched, with CTNNB1, AXIN1, LEF1 among leading genes—consistent with oncogenic Wnt activation in hotspot carriers.

Comparisons & Implications  
CTNNB1 mutations drive a shift toward enhanced proteostasis, translation and mitochondrial output, in parallel with suppression of immune and differentiation programs—consistent with a more proliferative, immune‐cold phenotype.  Downregulation of EMT and ciliary genes may reflect altered epithelial polarity and cell motility, implicating CTNNB1‐mutant EC in distinct invasion modes.  Therapeutic targeting of proteostasis (e.g., ER stress modulators) or mitochondrial metabolism may selectively affect CTNNB1-mutant tumors, while strategies to reactivate immune pathways (complement, NF-κB) could overcome immune evasion.

Next Steps & Clarification  
1. Validate CTNNB1 S45 phosphorylation loss at the protein level against phosphoproteomic data—correlate abundance changes with specific phosphosite regulation.  
2. Test whether ER stress inhibitors (e.g., HSP90 or proteasome modulators) preferentially affect viability of CTNNB1-mutant EC cell lines.  
3. Assess immune cell infiltration and complement activity in CTNNB1-mutant vs WT EC clinical specimens.  
4. Investigate whether suppression of EMT markers translates into altered migration/invasion phenotypes in vitro.
